quotes.text: You probably do not get enough sleep if you're constantly tired during the day.
You may be referred to a sleep clinic if you have symptoms of another sleep disorder such as sleep apnoea.

claims.reason: Only a part is backed: the NHS page says that sleep-disorder symptoms such as sleep apnoea can lead to a sleep clinic referral, and that constant daytime tiredness probably means too little sleep. Not backed: the specific advice to consult about marked sleepiness that persists despite adequate opportunity to sleep, and the advice not to rely only on more caffeine. The NHS page gives its 'See a GP' advice for insomnia (trouble sleeping), not for excessive sleepiness despite enough sleep opportunity, and says nothing about using caffeine against sleepiness (it lists caffeine only as a cause of insomnia). The Van Dongen abstract does not mention caffeine or consultation.

claims.reason: Both parts of the sentence (cumulative deficits at 4 h and 6 h; sleepiness ratings not reflecting them in full) have quotes. The abstract's wording on awareness is an interpretation by the authors ('suggest').

claims.claim: B — badania laboratoryjne z randomizacją oraz ogólna informacja NHS o potrzebie snu.

quotes.text: Both experiments were conducted under standardized laboratory conditions
The chronic sleep restriction experiment involved randomization to one of three sleep doses
How much sleep you need
adults need 7 to 9 hours

claims.reason: The grade letter B is editorial and was not checked; only the words after it were compared with the snapshots. Supported: both experiments were laboratory studies; the chronic sleep restriction experiment was randomised to three sleep doses; the NHS page has a general section on how much sleep adults need. Not supported by the abstract: the plural 'badania ... z randomizacją' implies that all the laboratory studies were randomised, but the abstract states randomisation only for the chronic sleep restriction experiment and describes the total sleep deprivation experiment only as 3 nights without sleep (0 h), with no statement on allocation. How randomisation was done needs the full text; the snapshot is an abstract.

quotes.text: still feel tired after waking up
Things that keep you from getting a good night's sleep:

claims.reason: Indirect support only. The NHS page lists feeling tired after waking as an insomnia symptom and lists conditions that keep you from a good night's sleep (noise, sleep apnoea and others), which fits the idea. It does not state that sleep quality matters in addition to the number of hours. The Van Dongen abstract varies time in bed and does not address sleep quality as a separate factor.

claims.claim: Badanie nie określa dokładnej potrzeby każdej osoby
claims.reason: This says that something was not measured. The Van Dongen snapshot is an abstract only (Europe PMC), and an abstract cannot show absence. It describes group-level doses assigned by randomisation, but whether the full text derives any individual sleep need needs the full text of the paper.

claims.claim: nie uzasadnia samodzielnego leczenia zaburzeń snu

scope_gaps.note: The sentence does not say that the total sleep deprivation arm was a separate 3-night experiment (0 h in bed); a reader may assume one experiment with all arms randomised.

The abstract describes healthy adults in a laboratory where all other sleep was prohibited; the sentence does not say this, and a reader may assume the result applies to everyday partial sleep loss outside the laboratory.
The NHS page gives GP advice for insomnia, not for marked daytime sleepiness despite adequate time for sleep. No snapshot compares consultation with caffeine.
Randomisation is stated only for the chronic sleep restriction experiment, not for the total sleep deprivation experiment; the grade letter B was not checked.
Neither snapshot states that sleep quality matters in addition to duration.
